blocks.note: Choose address forms and maintain French gender-number agreement for personal and collective referents.
Distinguish unspecified, passive-like, generic and speaker-inclusive on, including written l'on.
Retrieve entities with personal pronouns and events, states or classes with neutral ce, cela or ça.
Select formal impersonal il versus cela from fixed frames and the predicate's experiencer structure.
Contrast personal description with neutral identification and impersonal evaluation in il est and c'est frames.
Derive direct or indirect object form from the French verb and attach it to the verb that governs it.
Use neutral le for propositions and properties, then distinguish state-of-affairs and lexical pronominal se.
Separate ordinary à-preposition complements from indirect objects and apply the affected-body-part construction.
Replace non-human prepositional and de complements with y or en, retaining numerals and quantifiers.
Order multiple object pronouns before finite and infinitive verbs and after affirmative imperatives.
Use stressed forms for emphasis, standalone reference, prepositional complements and coordination.
